Study Notes  
THE BHARATIYA NYAYA  
SANHITA, 2023  
Chapter XII - XIX  
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  
OF OFFENCES BY OR RELATING TO PUBLIC SERVANTS CHAPTER XII SECTION 198-205  
.
PUBLIC SERVANT DISOBEYING LAW, WITH INTENT TO CAUSE INJURY TO ANY  
PERSON (Section 198):  

A public servant who intentionally disobeys the law on how to conduct themselves,  
with the intent or knowledge that it may cause harm, shall be punished with  
simple imprisonment for up to one year, or with fine, or with both.  
o Example: A, being an officer directed by law to take property in execution,  
in order to satisfy a decree pronounced in Z’s favour by a Court, knowingly  
disobeys that direction of law, with the knowledge that he is likely thereby  
to cause injury to Z. A has committed the offence defined in this section.  
.
PUBLIC SERVANT DISOBEYING DIRECTION UNDER LAW (Section 199):  

A public servant who:  
o knowingly disobeys the law, specifically directions preventing them from  
compelling someone's attendance for an investigation;  
o knowingly disobeys any law governing how they should conduct an  
investigation, causing harm or prejudice to any person;  
o fails to document information provided to them under section 173(1) of the  
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, concerning cognizable  
offenses listed under sections 64-68, 70-71, 74, 76, 77, 79, 124, 143 or  
144;  
shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a minimum of six months to a  
maximum of two years and shall also be liable to fine.  
.
.
PUNISHMENT FOR NONTREATMENT OF VICTIM (Section 200):  

Anyone overseeing a hospital, whether government or privately run, who violates  
section 397 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, shall be liable to  
be punished with imprisonment for up to one year, or with fine, or with both.  
PUBLIC SERVANT FRAMING AN INCORRECT DOCUMENT WITH INTENT TO CAUSE  
INJURY (Section 201):  

A public servant tasked with preparing or translating documents or electronic  
records, who intentionally creates them incorrectly with the knowledge or belief  
that it may cause harm, shall be punished with imprisonment for up to three  
years, or with fine, or with both.  
.
PUBLIC SERVANT UNLAWFULLY ENGAGING IN TRADE (Section 202):  

A public servant, legally obligated not to engage in trade, who violates this  
obligation shall be liable to punishment with simple imprisonment for up to  
one year, or with fine, or with both, or community service.  
2
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  
.
PUBLIC SERVANT UNLAWFULLY BUYING OR BIDDING FOR PROPERTY (Section  
203):  

A public servant, obligated not to buy or bid for specific property, who does so in  
their name or someone else's, individually or jointly, shall be liable to punishment  
with simple imprisonment for up to two years, or with fine, or with both.  
Additionally, the purchased property shall be confiscated.  
.
.
PERSONATING A PUBLIC SERVANT (Section 204):  

Anyone falsely claiming to hold a specific public servant office, knowing they don't,  
or impersonating someone else in such a position, and then acting or attempting  
to act in that capacity, shall be punished with imprisonment for a minimum of  
six months and a maximum of three years, along with a fine.  
WEARING GARB OR CARRYING TOKEN USED BY PUBLIC SERVANT WITH  
FRAUDULENT INTENT (Section 205):  

Wearing attire or carrying symbols resembling those of a specific class of public  
servants with the intent to be mistaken as a public servant of that class shall be  
punishable with imprisonment for up to three months, or with fine of up to  
five thousand rupees, or with both.  
OF CONTEMPTS OF THE LAWFUL AUTHORITY OF PUBLIC SERVANTS CHAPTER XIII  
SECTION 206-226  
.
ABSCONDING TO AVOID SERVICE OF SUMMONS OR OTHER PROCEEDING  
(Section 206):  

Anyone who goes into hiding to avoid receiving a summons, notice, or order from  
a legally competent public servant shall be punished with imprisonment for up  
to one month, or with fine of up to five thousand rupees, or with both.  

If the summons or notice is related to a Court appearance, producing a document,  
or an electronic record, the punishment shall be imprisonment for up to six  
months, a fine of up to ten thousand rupees, or with both.  
.
PREVENTING SERVICE OF SUMMONS OR OTHER PROCEEDING, OR PREVENTING  
PUBLICATION THEREOF (Section 207):  

Intentionally obstructing the delivery of a summons, notice, or order from a legally  
competent public servant, preventing lawful affixing or removal from an authorized  
place, or hindering the proclamation directed by a competent public servant shall  
be punished with simple imprisonment for up to one month, or with fine of  
up to five thousand rupees, or with both.  

If the summons, notice, order, or proclamation involves a court appearance,  
producing a document, or an electronic record, the penalty shall include  
3
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  
imprisonment for up to six months, or with fine of up to ten thousand rupees,  
or with both.  
.
NONATTENDANCE IN OBEDIENCE TO AN ORDER FROM PUBLIC SERVANT  
(Section 208):  

Anyone legally required to appear at a specific place and time in response to a  
summons, notice, order, or proclamation from a competent public servant, who  
intentionally fails to attend or leaves before the lawful time to depart shall be  
punished with simple imprisonment for up to one month, or with fine of up  
to five thousand rupees, or with both.  

For non-attendance or departure before the lawful time at a court-ordered  
appearance, whether in person or by agent, the penalty shall be imprisonment  
for up to six months, with fine of up to ten thousand rupees, or with both.  
o Example: A, being legally bound to appear before a High Court, in  
obedience to a subpoena issuing from that Court, intentionally omits to  
appear. A has committed the offence defined in this section.  
.
NONAPPEARANCE IN RESPONSE TO A PROCLAMATION UNDER SECTION 84 OF  
BHARATIYA NAGARIK SURAKSHA SANHITA, 2023 (Section 209):  

Anyone failing to appear at the specified place and time as required by a  
proclamation under section 84 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023,  
shall be punished with imprisonment for up to three years, or with fine, or  
with both, or community service.  
o If declared a proclaimed offender, the punishment shall extend to seven  
years and include fine.  
.
OMISSION TO PRODUCE DOCUMENT OR ELECTRONIC RECORD TO PUBLIC  
SERVANT BY PERSON LEGALLY BOUND TO PRODUCE IT (Section 210):  

Failure to produce or deliver a document or electronic record as legally required to  
a public servant shall be liable to punishment with imprisonment for up to one  
month, or with fine of up to five thousand rupees, or with both.  
For not producing or delivering a document or electronic record to a Court as  
legally required, the punishment shall be imprisonment for up to six months, or  
with fine of up to ten thousand rupees, or with both.  

o Example: A, being legally bound to produce a document before a District  
Court, intentionally omits to produce the same. A has committed the  
offence defined in this section.  
.
OMISSION TO GIVE NOTICE OR INFORMATION TO PUBLIC SERVANT BY PERSON  
LEGALLY BOUND TO GIVE IT (Section 211):  
4
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  


Intentionally omitting to provide notice or information to a public servant as legally  
required shall be punished with imprisonment for up to one month, or with  
fine of up to five thousand rupees, or with both.  
Failing to provide notice or information related to the commission of an offense, or  
for preventing its commission or apprehending an offender, the penalty shall be  
imprisonment for up to six months, or with fine of up to ten thousand rupees,  
or with both.  

For not providing notice or information as required by an order under section 394  
of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, the punishment shall be  
imprisonment for up to six months, or with fine of up to one thousand  
rupees, or with both.  
.
FURNISHING FALSE INFORMATION (Section 212):  

Providing false information to a public servant when legally obligated shall be  
punished with imprisonment for up to six months, or with fine of up to five  
thousand rupees, or with both.  

If the false information, which the person is legally obligated to provide, is related  
to the commission of an offense, or is required to prevent an offense or apprehend  
an offender, the punishment shall be imprisonment for up to two years, or with  
fine, or with both.  
o Example: A, a landholder, knowing of the commission of a murder within  
the limits of his estate, wilfully misinforms the Magistrate of the district that  
the death has occurred by accident in consequence of the bite of a snake.  
A is guilty of the offence defined in this section.  
NOTE:  
In sections 211 and this section 212, the term "offense" encompasses acts  
committed outside India that, if committed within India, would be punishable under  
specific sections. These sections include 103, 105, 307, subsections (2), (3), and (4) of  
section 309, subsections (2), (3), (4), and (5) of section 310, 311, 312, clauses (f) and (g)  
of section 326, subsections (4), (6), (7), and (8) of section 331, and clauses (a) and (b) of  
section 332. The term "offender" includes any person accused of such acts.  
.
REFUSING OATH OR AFFIRMATION WHEN DULY REQUIRED BY PUBLIC SERVANT  
TO MAKE IT (Section 213):  

Refusing to take an oath or affirmation to tell the truth when legally required by a  
competent public servant shall be punishable with imprisonment for up to six  
months, or with fine of up to five thousand rupees, or with both.  
.
REFUSING TO ANSWER PUBLIC SERVANT AUTHORISED TO QUESTION (Section  
214):  
5
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  

Refusing to truthfully answer a public servant's lawful question, when legally  
obligated, shall be punishable with imprisonment for up to six months, or with  
fine of up to five thousand rupees, or with both.  
.
.
REFUSING TO SIGN STATEMENT (Section 215):  

Refusing to sign a statement when legally required by a competent public servant  
shall be punishable with imprisonment for up to three months, or with fine  
of up to three thousand rupees, or with both.  
FALSE STATEMENT ON OATH OR AFFIRMATION TO PUBLIC SERVANT OR  
PERSON AUTHORISED TO ADMINISTER AN OATH OR AFFIRMATION (Section 216):  

Providing false information under oath to a public servant or another authorized  
person, when legally obligated to speak the truth, shall be punishable with  
imprisonment for up to three years and shall also be liable to fine.  
.
FALSE INFORMATION, WITH INTENT TO CAUSE PUBLIC SERVANT TO USE HIS  
LAWFUL POWER TO INJURY OF ANOTHER PERSON (Section 217):  

Providing false information to a public servant with the intention to:  
o act improperly or refrain from necessary actions by providing false  
information;  
o to use the lawful power of such public servant to the injury or annoyance  
of any person,  
shall be punishable with imprisonment for up to one year, or with fine of up to  
ten thousand rupees, or with both.  
Example: A informs a Magistrate that Z, a police officer,  
subordinate to such Magistrate, has been guilty of neglect of duty  
or misconduct, knowing such information to be false, and knowing  
it to be likely that the information will cause the Magistrate to  
dismiss Z. A has committed the offence defined in this section.  
.
.
RESISTANCE TO TAKING OF PROPERTY BY LAWFUL AUTHORITY OF A PUBLIC  
SERVANT (Section 218):  

Resisting the lawful authority of a public servant during the taking of any property  
shall be punishable with imprisonment for up to six months, or with fine of  
up to ten thousand rupees, or with both.  
OBSTRUCTING SALE OF PROPERTY OFFERED FOR SALE BY AUTHORITY OF  
PUBLIC SERVANT (Section 219):  

Intentionally obstructing the sale of property conducted by the lawful authority of a  
public servant shall be punishable with imprisonment for up to one month, or  
with fine of up to five thousand rupees, or with both.  
6
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  
.
ILLEGAL PURCHASE OR BID FOR PROPERTY OFFERED FOR SALE BY  
AUTHORITY OF PUBLIC SERVANT (Section 220):  

Purchasing or bidding for property on behalf of someone legally incapable or  
bidding without intending to fulfill the obligations at a public sale authorized by a  
public servant shall be punishable with imprisonment for up to one month, or  
with fine of up to two hundred rupees, or with both.  
.
.
OBSTRUCTING PUBLIC SERVANT IN DISCHARGE OF PUBLIC FUNCTIONS  
(Section 221):  

Voluntarily obstructing a public servant while performing their duties shall be  
punishable with imprisonment for up to three months, or with fine of up to  
two thousand and five hundred rupees, or with both.  
OMISSION TO ASSIST PUBLIC SERVANT WHEN BOUND BY LAW TO GIVE  
ASSISTANCE (Section 222):  

Failing to provide assistance to a public servant as required by law shall be  
punishable with simple imprisonment for up to one month, or with fine of up  
to two thousand and five hundred rupees, or with both.  

Refusing to provide assistance to a public servant when legally demanded for  
executing a court process, preventing an offence, suppressing a riot or affray, or  
apprehending an offender, shall be punishable with simple imprisonment for  
up to six months, or with fine of up to five thousand rupees, or with both.  
.
DISOBEDIENCE TO ORDER DULY PROMULGATED BY PUBLIC SERVANT (Section  
223):  

Disobeying a lawful order from a public servant, directing one to refrain from a  
specific act or take certain actions with particular property shall, if the disobedience  
results in:  
o obstruction, annoyance, or injury to anyone lawfully employed, the  
offender, be punished with simple imprisonment for up to six months,  
or with fine up to two thousand and five hundred rupees, or with both.  
o in endangering human life, health, or safety, or causes a riot or affray, the  
offender, shall be punished with imprisonment for up to one year, or with  
fine up to five thousand rupees, or with both.  

Intent to harm is not a requirement for the offense. It is enough if the offender  
is aware of the order, disobeys it, and this disobedience causes or is likely to cause  
harm.  
o Example: An order is promulgated by a public servant lawfully empowered  
to promulgate such order, directing that a religious procession shall not  
pass down a certain street. A knowingly disobeys the order, and thereby  
causes danger of riot. A has committed the offence defined in this section.  
7
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  
.
THREAT OF INJURY TO PUBLIC SERVANT (Section 224):  

Threatening a public servant or someone connected to them to influence their  
actions in the exercise of their public functions shall be punishable with  
imprisonment for up to two years, or with a fine, or with both.  
.
THREAT OF INJURY TO INDUCE PERSON TO REFRAIN FROM APPLYING FOR  
PROTECTION TO PUBLIC SERVANT (Section 225):  

Threatening a person to deter them from legally applying for protection against any  
injury to a public servant, who is legally empowered to provide such protection,  
shall be punishable with imprisonment for up to one year, or with a fine, or  
with both.  
.
ATTEMPT TO COMMIT SUICIDE TO COMPEL OR RESTRAIN EXERCISE OF LAWFUL  
POWER (Section 226):  

Attempting suicide with the intent to compel or restrain a public servant from  
discharging official duties shall be punishable with imprisonment for up to one  
year, or with a fine, or with both, or with community service.  
OF FALSE EVIDENCE AND OFFENCES AGAINST PUBLIC JUSTICE CHAPTER XIV  
SECTION 227-269  
.
GIVING FALSE EVIDENCE (Section 227):  



Giving false evidence refers to making a false statement under oath, violating  
a legal obligation to speak the truth or make a truthful declaration.  
A false statement, whether spoken or expressed in other forms, falls under this  
section.  
Additionally, making a false statement about one's belief is also considered  
giving false evidence. This includes falsely claiming to believe something one  
doesn't, similar to falsely asserting knowledge.  
o Example: A, in support of a just claim which B has against Z for one  
thousand rupees, falsely swears on a trial that he heard Z admit the justice  
of B’s claim. A has given false evidence.  
.
FABRICATING FALSE EVIDENCE (Section 228):  

Creating false circumstances, entries in records, or false statements in  
documents, electronic records, with the intention of presenting them as  
evidence in a judicial or legal proceeding, aiming to influence someone's  
opinion and potentially lead to a mistaken conclusion in that proceeding, is  
termed as "fabricating false evidence."  
o Example: A puts jewels into a box belonging to Z, with the intention that  
they may be found in that box, and that this circumstance may cause Z to  
be convicted of theft. A has fabricated false evidence.  
8
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  
.
PUNISHMENT FOR FALSE EVIDENCE (Section 229):  




Providing false evidence or creating fabricated evidence with the intent to use it in  
any stage of a judicial proceeding shall be punishable with imprisonment up to  
seven years and a fine of up to ten thousand rupees.  
Providing false evidence or creating fabricated evidence in any case, other than  
the one mentioned above, shall be punishable with imprisonment for up to  
three years and a fine of up to five thousand rupees.  
A trial before a Court-martial is considered a judicial proceeding. Additionally, an  
investigation mandated by law, even if it occurs outside of a Court, is  
regarded as a stage of a judicial proceeding.  
An investigation ordered by a Court in accordance with the law and  
conducted under the Court's authority is considered a stage of a judicial  
proceeding, even if the investigation itself doesn't occur within the Court premises.  
o Example:  
A, in an enquiry before a Magistrate for the purpose of ascertaining  
whether Z ought to be committed for trial, makes on oath a  
statement which he knows to be false. As this enquiry is a stage of  
a judicial proceeding, A has given false evidence.  
A, in an enquiry before an officer deputed by a Court to ascertain  
on the spot the boundaries of land, makes on oath a statement  
which he knows to be false. As this enquiry is a stage of a judicial  
proceeding, A has given false evidence.  
.
GIVING OR FABRICATING FALSE EVIDENCE WITH INTENT TO PROCURE  
CONVICTION OF CAPITAL OFFENCE (Section 230):  

If someone provides false evidence with the intention of causing the wrongful  
conviction of a person for a capital offense, they shall be punished with life  
imprisonment or rigorous imprisonment up to ten years, along with a fine of  
up to fifty thousand rupees.  

If an innocent person is wrongly convicted and executed due to false evidence, the  
person giving such false evidence shall be punished with either death or the  
penalty mentioned in the above provision.  
.
GIVING OR FABRICATING FALSE EVIDENCE WITH INTENT TO PROCURE  
CONVICTION OF OFFENCE PUNISHABLE WITH IMPRISONMENT FOR LIFE OR  
IMPRISONMENT (Section 231):  

If someone provides false evidence with the intention of getting someone  
convicted, or knowing that it could lead to conviction for a non-capital offense  
punishable by life imprisonment or at least seven years, they shall be punished  
as if they committed the offense themselves.  
o Example: A gives false evidence before a Court, intending thereby to cause  
Z to be convicted of a dacoity. The punishment of dacoity is imprisonment  
for life, or rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years,  
9
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  
with or without fine. A, therefore, is liable to imprisonment for life or  
imprisonment, with or without fine.  
.
THREATENING ANY PERSON TO GIVE FALSE EVIDENCE (Section 232):  

Anyone who threatens another person, intending to make them provide false  
evidence by causing harm to their person, reputation, or property, shall be  
punishable with imprisonment up to seven years, or with fine, or with both.  
If an innocent person is wrongly convicted and receives a death sentence or  
imprisonment exceeding seven years due to false evidence, the person who made  
the threats leading to the false evidence shall be punished with the same  
severity as the innocent person, in the same manner and to the same extent.  

.
.
USING EVIDENCE KNOWN TO BE FALSE (Section 233):  

Anyone who knowingly uses or tries to use false or fabricated evidence as if it were  
true shall be punished in the same way as if they had given or fabricated that  
false evidence.  
ISSUING OR SIGNING FALSE CERTIFICATE (Section 234):  

Anyone who issues or signs a certificate required by law, or related to a fact  
admissible in evidence, knowing or believing it to be false in any material aspect,  
shall be punished as if they had given false evidence.  
.
.
USING AS TRUE A CERTIFICATE KNOWN TO BE FALSE (Section 235):  

Anyone who corruptly uses or tries to use a certificate as if it were true, knowing it  
to be false in any material aspect, shall be punished in the same manner as if  
they had given false evidence.  
FALSE STATEMENT MADE IN DECLARATION WHICH IS BY LAW RECEIVABLE AS  
EVIDENCE (Section 236):  

Anyone who, in a declaration that a court, public servant, or authorized person is  
legally bound to accept as evidence, knowingly makes a false statement regarding  
a material point related to the purpose of the declaration, shall be punished in  
the same manner as if they had given false evidence.  
.
USING AS TRUE SUCH DECLARATION KNOWING IT TO BE FALSE (Section 237):  

Anyone who corruptly uses or attempts to use a declaration as if it were true,  
knowing it to be false in any material aspect, shall be punished in the same  
manner as if they had given false evidence.  
o Even if a declaration is deemed inadmissible due to some informality, it is  
still considered a declaration under the relevant sections.  
10  
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  
.
CAUSING DISAPPEARANCE OF EVIDENCE OF OFFENCE, OR GIVING FALSE  
INFORMATION TO SCREEN OFFENDER (Section 238):  

Anyone who, knowing or suspecting that a crime has occurred, intentionally  
makes evidence disappear to shield the offender from legal consequences,  
or provides false information about the offense with the same intention,  
shall:  
o if the known or believed offense is punishable with death, the person shall  
be punished with imprisonment for up to seven years and fined.  
o if the offense carries a punishment of life imprisonment or up to ten years,  
the punishment shall be imprisonment for up to three years along with a  
fine.  
o for offenses punishable with imprisonment for less than ten years, the  
punishment shall be imprisonment for up to one-fourth of the longest term  
prescribed for the offense, or a fine, or both.  
Example: A, knowing that B has murdered Z, assists B to hide the  
body with the intention of screening B from punishment. A is liable  
to imprisonment of either description for seven years, and also to  
fine.  
.
INTENTIONAL OMISSION TO GIVE INFORMATION OF OFFENCE BY PERSON  
BOUND TO INFORM (Section 239):  

Anyone who, knowing or suspecting that an offense has occurred, deliberately fails  
to provide information about that offense, which they are legally obligated to give,  
shall be punished with imprisonment for up to six months, or with fine that  
may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both.  
.
GIVING FALSE INFORMATION RESPECTING AN OFFENCE COMMITTED (Section  
240):  

Anyone who, knowing or having reason to believe that an offense has been  
committed, provides false information about that offense, which they know or  
believe to be untrue, shall be punished with imprisonment for up to two years,  
or with fine, or with both.  

In sections 238, 239, and this section, the term "offence" encompasses any act  
committed outside of India that, if carried out within India, would be  
punishable under specific sections, including 103, 105, 307, section 309 (2)  
(3) (4), sub-sections (2), (3), (4), and (5) of section 310, 311, 312, section 326 (f)  
(g), section 331 (4) (6) (7) (8), and section 332 (a) & (b).  
.
DESTRUCTION OF DOCUMENT OR ELECTRONIC RECORD TO PREVENT ITS  
PRODUCTION AS EVIDENCE (section 241):  

Anyone who hides, destroys, or alters a document or electronic record that they  
are legally obligated to produce as evidence in court or before a public servant,  
11  
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  
with the intent to prevent its use in legal proceedings, shall be punished with  
imprisonment for up to three years, or with fine up to five thousand rupees,  
or with both.  
.
.
FALSE PERSONATION FOR PURPOSE OF ACT OR PROCEEDING IN SUIT OR  
PROSECUTION (Section 242):  

Anyone who falsely impersonates another, and in that assumed identity makes  
any admission, statement, confesses judgment, issues a process, becomes bail or  
security, or performs any other act in a legal or criminal case, shall be punished  
with imprisonment for up to three years, or with fine, or with both.  
FRAUDULENT REMOVAL OR CONCEALMENT OF PROPERTY TO PREVENT ITS  
SEIZURE AS FORFEITED OR IN EXECUTION (Section 243):  

Anyone who fraudulently removes, conceals, transfers, or delivers any property or  
interest in property with the intention of preventing it from being taken as a  
forfeiture or to satisfy a fine under a court sentence, or to evade execution of a civil  
suit decree, shall be punished with imprisonment for up to three years, or with  
fine up to five thousand rupees, or with both.  
.
FRAUDULENT CLAIM TO PROPERTY TO PREVENT ITS SEIZURE AS FORFEITED  
OR IN EXECUTION (Section 244):  

Anyone who fraudulently accepts, receives, or claims any property or interest  
therein, knowing that they have no rightful claim to such property, or engages in  
deception regarding any right to the property or interest, with the intention of  
preventing it from being taken as a forfeiture or to satisfy a fine under a court  
sentence, or to evade execution of a civil suit decree, shall be punished with  
imprisonment for up to two years, or with fine, or with both.  
.
FRAUDULENTLY SUFFERING DECREE FOR SUM NOT DUE (Section 245):  

Anyone who fraudulently causes or allows a Court decree or order to be issued  
against them, falsely claiming a sum not due or a larger sum than owed, or for any  
property or interest to which the claimant is not entitled, or fraudulently allows the  
execution of a decree after it has been satisfied, shall be punished with  
imprisonment for up to two years, or with fine, or with both.  
o Example: A institutes a suit against Z. Z, knowing that A is likely to obtain  
a decree against him, fraudulently suffers a judgment to pass against him  
for a larger amount at the suit of B, who has no just claim against him, in  
order that B, either on his own account or for the benefit of Z, may share in  
the proceeds of any sale of Z’s property which may be made under A’s  
decree. Z has committed an offence under this section.  
.
DISHONESTLY MAKING FALSE CLAIM IN COURT (Section 246):  
12  
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  

Anyone who fraudulently, dishonestly, or with the intent to injure or annoy any  
person, makes a false claim in Court that they know to be untrue, shall be  
punished with imprisonment for up to two years and shall also be liable to  
pay a fine.  
.
FRAUDULENTLY OBTAINING DECREE FOR SUM NOT DUE (Section 247):  

Anyone who fraudulently obtains a Court decree or order against someone for a  
sum not owed, or for a larger sum than owed, or for any property or interest to  
which they are not entitled, or fraudulently causes the execution of a decree after  
it has been satisfied, or for anything in respect of which it has been satisfied, or  
allows such acts to be done in their name, shall be punished with imprisonment  
for up to two years, or with fine, or with both.  
.
FALSE CHARGE OF OFFENCE MADE WITH INTENT TO INJURE (Section 248):  

Anyone who, with the intent to cause harm to another person, initiates or causes  
the initiation of any criminal proceeding against that person or falsely accuses them  
of committing an offense, knowing that there is no just or lawful basis for such  
proceeding or charge, shall be punished with imprisonment for up to five  
years, or with fine up to two lakh rupees, or with both.  

If the false criminal proceeding is initiated with a charge of an offense punishable  
with death, life imprisonment, or imprisonment for ten years or more, the person  
responsible shall be punishable with imprisonment for up to ten years and  
shall also be liable to pay a fine.  
.
HARBOURING OFFENDER (Section 249):  

If someone hides a person they know or believe to be a criminal, with the intention  
of protecting them from punishment, and the offense is punishable by death, the  
person hiding them shall be imprisoned for up to five years and shall also be liable  
to fine.  


If the offense is punishable with life imprisonment or imprisonment up to ten years,  
the person harboring or concealing the offender shall be imprisoned for up to  
three years and may also be liable to pay a fine.  
If the offense is punishable with imprisonment for up to one year (but not exceeding  
ten years), those hiding the offender shall be liable to imprisonment of the kind  
specified for the offense, lasting up to one-fourth of the maximum  
imprisonment term allowed and shall also be fined or subjected to both  
imprisonment and fine.  

In this section, the term "offence" encompasses any act committed outside  
of India that, if committed within India, would be punishable under specific  
sections, including section 103, 105, 307, section 309 (2) (3) (4), sub-sections  
(2), (3), (4), and (5) of section 310, 311, 312, section 326 (f) & (g), section 331 (4)  
13  
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  
(6) (7) (8), and section 332 (a) & (b). For the purposes of this section, such acts  
are treated as if the accused person had committed them in India.  
o Example: A, knowing that B has committed dacoity, knowingly conceals B  
in order to screen him from legal punishment. Here, as B is liable to  
imprisonment for life, A is liable to imprisonment of either description for a  
term not exceeding three years, and is also liable to fine  
NOTE:  
This section shall not extend to any case in which the harbour or concealment is by the spouse  
of the offender  
.
TAKING GIFT, ETC., TO SCREEN AN OFFENDER FROM PUNISHMENT (Section  
250):  

Anyone who accepts, tries to obtain, or agrees to accept any gratification for  
themselves or another person, or any restitution of property for themselves or  
another person, in exchange for concealing an offense, shielding someone from  
legal punishment, or refraining from initiating legal proceedings against  
someone for the purpose of bringing them to legal punishment shall:  
o if the crime is punishable by death, they shall be imprisoned for up to seven  
years and fined; or  
o if the crime is punishable by life imprisonment or up to ten years, they shall  
be imprisoned for up to three years and fined; or  
o if the crime is punishable by imprisonment for less than ten years, they shall  
be imprisoned for a quarter of the maximum term, or fined, or both.  
.
OFFERING GIFT OR RESTORATION OF PROPERTY IN CONSIDERATION OF  
SCREENING OFFENDER (Section 251):  

Anyone providing, causing, offering, or agreeing to give gratification or restoring  
property to someone, in exchange for that person concealing an offense, shielding  
someone from legal punishment, or refraining from pursuing legal action against  
someone for the purpose of bringing them to legal punishment shall:  
o if the offense is punishable with death, the person shall be imprisoned for  
up to seven years and fined; or  
o if the offense is punishable with life imprisonment or up to ten years, the  
person shall be imprisoned for up to three years and fined; or  
o if the offense is punishable with imprisonment for less than ten years, the  
person shall be imprisoned for up to one-fourth of the longest term or fined,  
or both.  

Exception: These provisions do not apply if the offense can lawfully be settled or  
compounded, as per section 250.  
.
TAKING GIFT TO HELP TO RECOVER STOLEN PROPERTY, ETC. (Section 252):  
14  
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  

Anyone who accepts or agrees to take any gratification under the pretense or on  
account of assisting someone in recovering any movable property, which was  
unlawfully taken from them under an offense punishable under this code, shall be  
punished with imprisonment for up to two years, or fined, or both, unless  
they actively work to apprehend and ensure the conviction of the offender.  
.
HARBOURING OFFENDER WHO HAS ESCAPED FROM CUSTODY OR WHOSE  
APPREHENSION HAS BEEN ORDERED (Section 253):  

If a person convicted or charged with an offense escapes from lawful custody or a  
public servant orders someone's arrest for an offense, anyone who knowingly  
harbors or conceals that person with the intention of preventing their apprehension  
shall:  
o if the offense for which the person was in custody or is ordered to be  
apprehended is punishable with death, the offender shall be punished with  
imprisonment for up to seven years and fined; or  
o if the offense is punishable with life imprisonment or imprisonment for ten  
years, the offender shall be punished with imprisonment for up to three  
years, with or without a fine; or  
o if the offense is punishable with imprisonment ranging from one year to less  
than ten years, the offender shall be punished with imprisonment of the  
type provided for that offense, for up to one-fourth of the longest term of  
imprisonment allowed for such offense, or fined, or both.  


In this section, "offence" also includes any act or omission for which a person  
is alleged to have been guilty outside of India. If the same act or omission, if  
committed in India, would have been punishable as an offence, and the person is,  
under any law related to extradition or otherwise, liable to be apprehended or  
detained in custody in India, then every such act or omission is deemed punishable  
under this section as if the accused person had been guilty of it in India.  
Exception: This section does not apply when the harboring or concealment is  
done by the spouse of the person to be apprehended.  
.
.
PUBLIC SERVANT DISOBEYING DIRECTION OF LAW WITH INTENT TO SAVE  
PERSON FROM PUNISHMENT OR PROPERTY FROM FORFEITURE (Section 255):  

If a public servant knowingly disobeys the law related to their conduct with the  
intention of saving someone from legal punishment, subjecting them to a lesser  
punishment, or saving property from forfeiture or charges, they shall be punished  
with imprisonment for up to two years, a fine, or both.  
PUBLIC SERVANT FRAMING INCORRECT RECORD OR WRITING WITH INTENT TO  
SAVE PERSON FROM PUNISHMENT OR PROPERTY FROM FORFEITURE (Section  
256):  

If a public servant, entrusted with preparing any record or writing, intentionally  
creates it inaccurately, knowing that it may cause loss or injury to the public or any  
15  
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  
person, or with the intent to save someone from legal punishment or protect  
property from forfeiture, they shall be punished with imprisonment for up to  
three years, or with fine, or with both.  
.
.
PUBLIC SERVANT IN JUDICIAL PROCEEDING CORRUPTLY MAKING REPORT,  
ETC., CONTRARY TO LAW (Section 257):  

A public servant who, corruptly or maliciously, makes or pronounces any report,  
order, verdict, or decision in any stage of a judicial proceeding, knowing it to be  
contrary to law, shall be punished with imprisonment for up to seven years, or  
with fine, or with both.  
COMMITMENT FOR TRIAL OR CONFINEMENT BY PERSON HAVING AUTHORITY  
WHO KNOWS THAT HE IS ACTING CONTRARY TO LAW (Section 258):  

Any person holding an office that grants legal authority to commit individuals for  
trial or confinement, or to keep individuals in confinement, who corruptly or  
maliciously commits or keeps a person in confinement, knowing that such actions  
are contrary to the law, shall be punished with imprisonment for up to seven  
years, or with fine, or with both.  
.
INTENTIONAL OMISSION TO APPREHEND ON PART OF PUBLIC SERVANT BOUND  
TO APPREHEND (Section 259):  

A public servant who, legally obligated to apprehend or keep in confinement  
any person charged with or liable to be apprehended for an offense,  
intentionally fails to apprehend, allows the person to escape, or aids in their  
escape, shall be subject to punishment:  
o if the offense is punishable with death, the public servant shall be liable to  
punishment of imprisonment for up to seven years, with or without a fine;  
or  
o if the offense is punishable with life imprisonment or imprisonment for up  
to ten years, the public servant shall be liable to punishment of  
imprisonment for up to three years, with or without a fine; or  
o if the offense is punishable with imprisonment for a term less than ten  
years, the public servant shall be liable to punishment of imprisonment for  
up to two years, with or without a fine.  
.
INTENTIONAL OMISSION TO APPREHEND ON PART OF PUBLIC SERVANT BOUND  
TO APPREHEND PERSON UNDER SENTENCE OR LAWFULLY COMMITTED  
(Section 260):  

A public servant, who is legally obligated to apprehend or keep in  
confinement any person under sentence of a Court for an offense or lawfully  
committed to custody, but intentionally omits to apprehend, allows escape, or  
aids in the escape of such person, shall be subjected to punishment:  
16  
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  
o for a public servant, who intentionally omits to apprehend or allows the  
escape of a person under sentence of death, shall be imprisonment for life  
or imprisonment for a term which may extend to fourteen years, with or  
without a fine; or  
o for a public servant who intentionally fails to apprehend or allows the  
escape of a person sentenced to life imprisonment or ten years or more  
shall be liable to imprisonment for up to seven years, with or without a fine;  
or  
o for a public servant intentionally omitting to apprehend or aiding the escape  
of a person sentenced to less than ten years or lawfully in custody shall be  
punished with imprisonment for up to three years, or with fine, or with both.  
.
.
ESCAPE FROM CONFINEMENT OR CUSTODY NEGLIGENTLY SUFFERED BY  
PUBLIC SERVANT (Section 261):  

A public servant, who is legally obligated to keep a person charged with or  
convicted of an offense in confinement but negligently allows that person to  
escape, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for up to two years, or  
with fine, or with both.  
RESISTANCE OR OBSTRUCTION BY A PERSON TO HIS LAWFUL APPREHENSION  
(Section 262):  

Anyone who intentionally resists or obstructs the lawful apprehension for an  
offense they are charged with or convicted of, or escapes or attempts to escape  
from lawful custody for such an offense, shall be punished with imprisonment  
for up to two years, or with fine, or with both.  
o The punishment specified herein is in addition to any other punishment that  
the person to be apprehended or detained in custody was liable for the  
offense with which they were charged or convicted.  
.
RESISTANCE OR OBSTRUCTION TO LAWFUL APPREHENSION OF ANOTHER  
PERSON (Section 263):  

Anyone who intentionally resists or unlawfully obstructs the lawful  
apprehension of another person for an offense or rescues, or attempts to  
rescue, another person from lawful custody in which they are detained for an  
offense shall:  
o be imprisonment for upto two years, or with fine, or with both; or  
o if the person to be apprehended, or rescued or attempted to be rescued, is  
charged with or liable to be apprehended for an offense punishable with:  
imprisonment for life or imprisonment for a term up to ten years, the  
punishment shall be imprisonment of either description for up to  
three years, and also liable to a fine; or  
death, the punishment shall be imprisonment of either description  
for up to seven years, and also liable to a fine; or  
17  
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  
o if the person to be apprehended, rescued, or attempted to be rescued is:  
liable under the sentence of a Court or by virtue of a commutation  
of such a sentence to imprisonment for life or imprisonment for a  
term of ten years or upwards, the punishment shall be imprisonment  
of either description for up to seven years, and also liable to a fine;  
or  
under a death sentence, the punishment shall be imprisonment for  
life or for a term not exceeding ten years, along with a fine.  
.
OMISSION TO APPREHEND, OR SUFFERANCE OF ESCAPE, ON PART OF PUBLIC  
SERVANT, IN CASES NOT OTHERWISE PROVIDED FOR (Section 264):  

A public servant who fails to apprehend or allows the escape of a person,  
where specific provisions are not covered in sections 259-261, shall be punished:  
o if does so intentionally, shall be punished with imprisonment for up to three  
years, or with fine, or with both;  
o if he does so negligently, the punishment shall be simple imprisonment for  
up to two years, or with fine, or with both.  
.
RESISTANCE OR OBSTRUCTION TO LAWFUL APPREHENSION OR ESCAPE OR  
RESCUE IN CASES NOT OTHERWISE PROVIDED FOR (Section 265):  

If a person intentionally resists, obstructs lawful apprehension, escapes, or  
attempts to escape custody, or rescues or attempts to rescue another person from  
lawful detention, and the case is not covered by other specific laws, they shall be  
punished with imprisonment of either description for up to six months, or  
with fine, or with both.  
.
VIOLATION OF CONDITION OF REMISSION OF PUNISHMENT (Section 266):  

If a person, having accepted conditional remission of punishment, knowingly  
violates any condition on which such remission was granted, they shall be  
punished with the original sentence if they have not yet served any part of it. If they  
have already served a portion of the original sentence, they shall be punished  
with the remaining part of the original sentence that they have not yet  
undergone.  
.
.
INTENTIONAL INSULT OR INTERRUPTION TO PUBLIC SERVANT SITTING IN  
JUDICIAL PROCEEDING (Section 267):  

If someone intentionally insults or interrupts a public servant during a judicial  
proceeding, they shall be punished with simple imprisonment for up to six  
months, or with fine up to five thousand rupees, or with both.  
PERSONATION OF ASSESSOR (Section 268):  
18  
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  

If someone intentionally causes or allows themselves to be included as an  
assessor in a case, knowing that they are not legally entitled to be included or, if  
already included, knowingly continues to serve as an assessor contrary to the law,  
they shall be punished with imprisonment for up to two years, or with a fine,  
or with both.  
.
FAILURE BY PERSON RELEASED ON BAIL BOND OR BOND TO APPEAR IN COURT  
(Section 269):  

If an individual, who has been charged with an offence and released on bail bond  
or on bond, fails to appear in court without sufficient cause (with the burden of  
proving the cause lying upon them), they shall be punished with imprisonment  
for a term up to one year, or with a fine, or with both.  

The punishment under this section is:  
o in addition to the punishment the offender would face upon conviction for  
the charged offence; and  
o without prejudice to the power of the Court to order forfeiture of the bond.  
OF AFFECTING THE PUBLIC HEALTH, SAFETY, CONVENIENCE, DECENCY AND  
MORALS CHAPTER XV SECTION 270-297  
19  
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  
OF OFFENCES RELATING TO RELIGION CHAPTER XVI SECTION 298-302  
.
SAME PROVISIONS AS IN IPC.  
OF OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY CHAPTER XVII SECTION 303-332  
.
.
The Indian Constitution recognizes and guarantees the right to property for citizens.  
Property is seen as an extension of an individual's personality, and protecting it brings  
satisfaction. This chapter serves to deter and penalize offenders while securing  
individuals' right to property.  
20  
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  
.
OF THEFT (Section 303):  

Theft is when someone moves another person's property without  
permission, intending to take it dishonestly.  

Theft applies to movable property, not things attached to the earth. Once  
detached, it can be stolen.  


If a theft involves moving and severing at the same time, it still qualifies as theft.  
Making something move by removing obstacles or separating it from another  
thing constitutes theft.  


If a person makes an animal move, they are considered to have moved  
everything influenced by that animal's motion.  
Consent for possession can be express or implied, given by the person in  
possession or someone with authority for that purpose.  
o Example: A cuts down a tree on Z’s ground, with the intention of dishonestly  
taking the tree out of Z’s possession without Z’s consent. Here, as soon as  
A has severed the tree in order to such taking, he has committed theft.  
21  
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  
THEFT INGREDIENTS  
.
MOVABLE PROPERTY: To constitute theft, the property must be movable,  
capable of being carried. Immovable property, permanently attached to the  
earth, is not subject to theft until it is severed and becomes movable without  
the owner's consent. Example, a standing tree is immovable, but once cut  
down, it becomes movable.  
In the case of Pyarelal Bhargava v., the State of Rajasthan, the  
Court ruled that even temporary removal of property with the intent to restore  
it constitutes theft, challenging the notion that theft requires a permanent loss.  
.
POSSESED BY SOMEONE: For theft to occur, the stolen property must be in  
the possession of another person. Mere intention to take property dishonestly  
is not an offense; actual removal from another person's possession is crucial.  
The case of Rakesh v. State of NCT of Delhi emphasized that until  
the property is physically taken, no offense has been committed, aligning with  
Section 378 of the IPC (BNS S. 303)  
.
.
.
INTENT TO DISHONESTLY TAKE IT: Dishonest intention is a crucial element  
in theft. Taking property alone is not considered theft; it must be accompanied  
by an intention to cause wrongful gain to one person and wrongful loss to  
another. The dishonest intent to benefit oneself at the expense of another is  
what defines theft.  
WITHOUT THE PERSON’S CONSENT: Taking someone's property without  
their prior consent, whether expressed or implied, constitutes theft. The offense  
occurs when the property is taken dishonestly and without the owner's consent.  
The key elements are the lack of permission and the dishonest intent of the  
offender.  
MOVING IT WITH THE AIM OF TAKING: Moving a property with a dishonest  
intention is the initial stage of committing theft. The act of moving the property  
is essential for the offense to be committed. The combination of dishonest  
intent and the physical movement of the property constitutes the crime of theft.  
.
Punishment:  

Anyone committing theft shall be punished with imprisonment up to three  
years, or with fine, or with both.  

Second or subsequent conviction, the punishment includes rigorous  
imprisonment ranging from one to five years, along with a fine.  
22  
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  
.
In cases where the stolen property is valued at less than five thousand rupees and  
it's the first offense, the person, upon returning or restoring the property, shall be  
sentenced to community service instead of imprisonment.  
.
SNATCHING (Section 304):  

Snatching is a type of theft where the offender forcefully seizes movable  
property from a person.  

Punishment: Sentenced to up to three years in prison and shall also be fined.  
.
OF EXTORTION (Section 308):  

Extortion occurs when someone intentionally instills fear of harm to a person  
or others, compelling them to hand over property, valuable security, or anything  
that can be converted into a valuable security.  
o Example: A threatens to publish a defamatory libel concerning Z unless Z  
gives him money. He thus induces Z to give him money. A has committed  
extortion.  

Punishment: Imprisonment up to seven years, or with fine, or with both.  
23  
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  
.
OF ROBBERY AND DACOITY (Section 309):  


In all cases of robbery, there is either theft or extortion.  
Theft Becomes Robbery:  
o if, during the theft or its commission, the offender voluntarily causes or  
attempts to cause death, hurt, wrongful restraint, or instills fear of instant  
death, instant hurt, or instant wrongful restraint to any person.  

Extortion Becomes Robbery:  
o when, during the act, the offender is present with the person put in fear.  
o The offender induces fear of instant death, instant hurt, or instant wrongful  
restraint, compelling the person in fear to deliver the extorted item.  
o Presence is established if the offender is close enough to create fear of  
instant harm or restraint.  
NOTE:  
24  
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  
In essence, robbery encompasses situations where theft or extortion is accompanied by  
the threat or use of force, injury, or fear.  
o Example: A holds Z down, and fraudulently takes Z’s money and jewels  
from Z’s clothes, without Z’s consent. Here A has committed theft, and, in  
order to the committing of that theft, has voluntarily caused wrongful  
restraint to Z. A has therefore committed robbery.  

Punishment:  
.
DACOITY (Section 310):  
Dacoity is when five or more people work together to commit or attempt  

robbery. It includes those actively involved in the act and those present and aiding  
the commission or attempt.  
There is no difference between the robbery and dacoity, except for the number of  
offenders. Group of people which is five or more than five in number makes an attempt to  
commit robbery or aids in committing or attempting a robbery, is said to commit dacoity.  

In the case of Amrish Devnarayan v. the State of Gujarat, the Court ruled that  
to establish dacoity, certain facts must be proven:  
o involvement of five or more persons as accused in the commission of the  
offense;  
o the attempt to commit the offense or the actual commission of the offense  
should be a joint effort.  
o these essential facts need to be demonstrated in Court to establish the  
crime of dacoity.  

Punishment:  
25  
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  
OF CRIMINAL MISAPPROPRIATION OF PROPERTY  
.
DISHONEST MISAPPROPRIATION OF PROPERTY (Section 314):  

Anyone who dishonestly misappropriates or converts movable property for  
personal use shall be punished with imprisonment, ranging from a minimum  
of six months to a maximum of two years, along with a fine.  
o Example: A takes property belonging to Z out of Z’s possession, in good  
faith believing at the time when he takes it, that the property belongs to  
himself. A is not guilty of theft; but if A, after discovering his mistake,  
dishonestly appropriates the property to his own use, he is guilty of an  
offence under this section.  

In the case of Ramaswami Nadar v. the State of Maharashtra, the Hon'ble  
Supreme Court clarified that the phrase "converts to his own use" in Section 403  
of IPC implies that the accused has utilized the property in a manner that  
goes against the rights of the property owner. This emphasizes that any use  
of the property by the accused should be in violation of the owner's rights to  
constitute an offense under this section.  
26  
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  


A dishonest misappropriation for a time only is a misappropriation within the  
meaning of this section.  
o Example: A finds a Government promissory note belonging to Z, bearing a  
blank endorsement. A, knowing that the note belongs to Z, pledges it with  
a banker as a security for a loan, intending at a future time to restore it to  
Z. A has committed an offence under this section.  
If a person finds property with no owner around and takes it to protect or  
return it, it's not considered dishonest misappropriation. However, if they later  
use it for themselves without trying to find the owner, it becomes an offense.  
o The concept of "reasonable means" and "reasonable time" is subjective  
and depends on the circumstances. The finder doesn't need to know the  
specific owner; it's enough if, at the time of taking, they don't believe it's  
their own or genuinely believe the real owner can't be found.  
o Example:  
A finds a rupee on the high road, not knowing to whom the rupee  
belongs, A picks up the rupee. Here A has not committed the  
offence defined in this section.  
A finds a letter on the road, containing a bank-note. From the  
direction and contents of the letter he learns to whom the note  
belongs. He appropriates the note. He is guilty of an offence under  
this section.  
27  
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  
OF CRIMINAL BREACH OF TRUST  
.
CRIMINAL BREACH OF TRUST (Section 316):  

Any person entrusted with property or having control over it, who  
dishonestly misappropriates, converts it for personal use, or violates the  
prescribed mode of trust discharge, commits criminal breach of trust. This  
includes dishonest use or disposal contrary to legal directions or contracts,  
whether express or implied, and allowing someone else to do so willfully.  
o Example: A, a carrier, is entrusted by Z with property to be carried by land  
or by water. A dishonestly misappropriates the property. A has committed  
criminal breach of trust.  

In the case of Shiva Sagar Tiwari v. Union of India, the Supreme Court ruled  
that a minister, in handling public property, holds the position of a trustee. It is the  
minister's duty to deal justly and fairly with public property. Failure to do so  
can lead to liability for criminal breach of trust. This underscores the  
responsibility of public officials to act in the best interests of the public when  
entrusted with public resources.  
28  
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  
OF RECEIVING STOLEN PROPERTY  
.
STOLEN PROPERTY (Section 317):  

Stolen property includes assets transferred through theft, extortion, robbery,  
cheating, or criminal misappropriation or breach of trust, regardless of whether  
the actions occurred within or outside India. However, if the property later  
falls into the possession of someone legally entitled to it, it is no longer  
considered stolen.  
OF CHEATING  
29  
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  
.
CHEATING (Section 318):  

Anyone who, through deception, fraudulently induces another person to  
deliver property, consent to retaining property, or engage in actions that  
cause harm is considered to have committed cheating.  

Dishonest concealment of facts is considered deception under this section.  
o Explanation: A, by falsely pretending to be in the Civil Service, intentionally  
deceives Z, and thus dishonestly induces Z to let him have on credit goods  
for which he does not mean to pay. A cheats.  

Punishment:  
.
CHEATING BY PERSONATION (Section 219):  

A person commits the offense of cheating by personation if they deceive others  
by pretending to be someone else, knowingly substituting one person for  
another, or representing that they or someone else is a person other than  
their true identity.  

It does not matter if the person being impersonated is real or imaginary; the  
offense is still committed.  
30  
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  

In the case of Sushil Kumar Datta v. State of West Bengal, the accused falsely  
presented himself as a Schedule Caste candidate during an IAS examination,  
leading to his selection and appointment. The Court ruled that the conviction  
under Section 420 of IPC (related to cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of  
property) is justified, holding the accused liable for his false representation.  
o Example: A cheats by pretending to be a certain rich banker of the same  
name. A cheats by personation.  
OF FRAUDULENT DEEDS AND DISPOSITIONS OF PROPERTY  
.
The offenses under this category pertain to unlawful actions concerning debts owed  
to creditors, as well as the transfer of assets and liabilities. This legal framework is  
designed to safeguard the interests of creditors and bona fide purchasers, among  
others.  
OF MISCHIEF  
MISCHIEF (Section 324):  
.



A person commits mischief when, with the intent to cause wrongful loss or  
damage to the public or any person, or knowing that such harm is likely, they  
cause the destruction of any property or make changes to it that diminish its  
value, utility, or adversely affect it.  
For the offense of mischief, it is not necessary for the offender to intend harm  
specifically to the owner of the damaged property. It is sufficient if the intent  
is to cause wrongful loss or damage to any person, whether or not they are  
the owner of the property.  
Mischief can be committed by an act affecting property belonging solely to  
the person committing the act or property owned jointly by that person and  
others.  
o Example: A voluntarily burns a valuable security belonging to Z intending  
to cause wrongful loss to Z. A has committed mischief.  
31  
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  

Punishment:  
o Guilty of committing mischief shall be punished with imprisonment up to  
six months, or with fine, or with both.  
OF CRIMINAL TRESPASS  
.
CRIMINAL TRESPASS AND HOUSE-TRESPASS (Section 329):  

A person is said to commit criminal trespass if they enter or go upon another  
person's property with the intent to commit an offense, intimidate, insult, or  
annoy anyone in possession of the property. This offense also includes  
unlawfully remaining on the property with the intent to intimidate, insult, annoy, or  
commit an offense after lawfully entering the premises.  
32  
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  

A person commits house-trespass if they enter or remain in any building,  
tent, or vessel used as a human dwelling, or any building used for worship  
or as a place for the custody of property. The introduction of any part of the  
trespasser's body is sufficient to constitute house-trespass.  


Punishment for Criminal Trespass: Imprisonment up to three months, or with  
fine up to five thousand rupees, or with both.  
Punishment for House Trespass: Imprisonment up to one year, or with fine up  
to five thousand rupees, or with both.  
OF OFFENCES R ELATING TO O DOCUMENTS AND TO PROPERTY MARKS  
CHAPTER XVIII SECTION 335-348  
.
MAKING A FALSE DOCUMENT (Section 335):  

Making False Documents or Electronic Records: A person is guilty of making  
false documents or electronic records if:  
o Creation with Intent to Deceive:  
Dishonestly or fraudulently makes, signs, seals, or executes a  
document or part of a document.  
Makes or transmits any electronic record or part of it.  
Affixes any electronic signature on any electronic record.  
Makes any mark denoting document execution or electronic  
signature authenticity.  
Intentionally creates the false impression that it was made, signed,  
sealed, executed, transmitted, or affixed by someone authorized,  
when it was not.  
33  
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  
o Unauthorized Alteration: Dishonestly or fraudulently alters a document or  
electronic record in a significant part, without lawful authority, after its  
creation.  
o Deceptive Influence: Dishonestly or fraudulently induces someone, who  
is mentally incapacitated or deceived, to sign, seal, execute, or alter a  
document or electronic record or to affix their electronic signature, knowing  
they are unaware of the content due to unsoundness of mind, intoxication,  
or deception.  
Example: A has a letter of credit upon B for rupees 10,000, written  
by Z. A, in order to defraud B, adds cipher to the 10,000, and makes  
the sum 1,00,000 intending that it may be believed by B that Z so  
wrote the letter. A has committed forgery.  


A man’s signature of his own name may amount to forgery.  
o Example: A signs his own name to a bill of exchange, intending that it may  
be believed that the bill was drawn by another person of the same name.  
A has committed forgery.  
Creating a false document using the name of a fictitious person, with the  
intention of making it appear as if the document was made by a real person, or  
using the name of a deceased person, with the intention of making it appear as if  
the document was made during their lifetime, can amount to forgery.  
o Example: A draws a bill of exchange upon a fictitious person, and  
fraudulently accepts the bill in the name of such fictitious person with intent  
to negotiate it. A commits forgery.  
NOTE:  
In this section, the term "affixing electronic signature" carries the meaning assigned to  
it in clause (d) of sub-section (1) of section 2 of the Information Technology Act, 2000.  
.
.
FORGERY (Section 336):  
A person commits forgery if they make any false document or false electronic  

record, or any part thereof, with the intent to cause damage or injury to the  
public or any person, to support any claim or title, to induce someone to part  
with property, or to enter into any express or implied contract, or with the  
intent to commit fraud or enable the commission of fraud.  
FORGED DOCUMENT OR ELECTRONIC RECORD AND USING IT AS GENUINE  
(Section 340):  

A document or electronic record made wholly or partially by forgery is termed  
a forged document or electronic record.  
34  
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  

Anyone who fraudulently or dishonestly uses a document or electronic record,  
knowing or having reason to believe it is forged, shall be punished as if they had  
forged it themselves.  
OF PROPERTY MARKS  
PROPERTY MARK (SECTION 345):  
.

A mark used for denoting that movable property belongs to a particular  
person is called a property mark.  

Anyone who marks movable property, goods, or any container like a case or  
package, in a way that reasonably leads others to believe that the marked  
property or goods, or the contents of the marked receptacle, belong to  
someone to whom they do not actually belong, is said to use a false property  
mark.  
35  
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  
OF CRIMINAL INTIMIDATION, INSULT, ANNOYANCE, DEFAMATION, ETC.  
CHAPTER XIX SECTION 351-356  
.
CRIMINAL INTIMIDATION (Section 351):  

A person commits criminal intimidation if they threaten another using any  
means, with the intent to cause harm to the person, their reputation, or their  
property, or to the person or reputation of someone the individual cares  
about.  


The aim is to create alarm, force the person to perform an act they are not legally  
obligated to do, or prevent them from doing an act they are legally entitled to do,  
as a means of avoiding the execution of the threat.  
A threat to injure the reputation of any deceased person in whom the person  
threatened is interested, is within this section.  
o Example: A, for the purpose of inducing B to resist from prosecuting a civil  
suit, threatens to burn B’s house. A is guilty of criminal intimidation.  
OF DEFAMATION  
.
Making or publishing any imputation about a person through spoken or written  
words, signs, or visible representations, with the intent to harm or with knowledge  
or reason to believe that it will harm the reputation of that person, constitutes  
defamation.  
o Defamation of Deceased Persons: Defamation may be applicable even  
to imputations about a deceased person if such imputation would harm the  
reputation of the person if they were alive. This is particularly relevant if the  
intention is to cause hurt to the feelings of the deceased person's family or  
close relatives.  
36  
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  
o Defamation of Companies or Associations: Making an imputation  
concerning a company, association, or a group of persons as a collective  
entity may also amount to defamation. This extends the scope of  
defamation to include harm to the reputation of not only individuals but also  
corporate entities or groups.  
o Irony or Alternative Imputations in Defamation: An imputation  
presented in the form of an alternative or expressed ironically may still be  
considered defamation. This provision recognizes that the manner in which  
an imputation is framed, even if presented as an alternative or ironic  
statement, can still have defamatory implications and be subject to legal  
consequences.  
o Criteria for Harmful Imputation: For an imputation to be considered  
harmful to a person's reputation, it must, either directly or indirectly, in the  
eyes of others:  
Lower the moral or intellectual character of the person.  
Lower the character of the person in respect of their caste or calling.  
Lower the credit of the person.  
Cause others to believe that the body of the person is in a  
loathsome or generally disgraceful state.  
o Example: A says— “Z is an honest man; he never stole B’s watch”;  
intending to cause it to be believed that Z did steal B’s watch. This is  
defamation, unless it falls within one of the exceptions.  
.
Exceptions: Certain cases may be exempted as per specific exceptions outlined  
elsewhere in the law as under:  
o Truth as a Defense in Defamation: Truth serves as a defense in  
defamation cases. If an imputation is true concerning any person and is  
deemed to be for the public good, it is not considered defamation. The  
determination of whether it is for the public good is a factual question that  
needs to be assessed in each specific case.  
o Protection for Expressing Opinion on Public Servants: Expressing an  
opinion in good faith about the conduct of a public servant in the discharge  
of their public functions, or about their character as revealed through that  
conduct, is not considered defamation. This provision protects individuals  
who, in good faith, express opinions on the performance and character of  
public servants within the scope of their official duties.  
o Protection for Expressing Opinion on Public Questions: Expressing an  
opinion in good faith about the conduct of any person regarding a public  
question, and about their character as revealed through that conduct  
(within the scope of that public question), is not considered defamation.  
This provision safeguards the expression of opinions on matters of public  
concern, as long as the opinions are made in good faith and are relevant  
to the public question at hand.  
37  
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023  
o Reporting Court Proceedings: Publishing a substantially true report of  
the proceedings of a court or the result of such proceedings is not  
considered defamation. This exception recognizes the importance of  
accurately reporting legal proceedings and outcomes without constituting  
defamation, provided the report is substantially true.  
o Inquiry by Magistrate as a Court: A Magistrate or another officer  
conducting an inquiry in an open court as a preliminary step to a trial in a  
court is considered a court within the context of the relevant section.  
o Opinion on Decided Cases: Expressing, in good faith, an opinion about  
the merits of any case, whether civil or criminal, that has been decided by  
a court is not defamation. Similarly, sharing an opinion about the conduct  
of any person involved in the case (party, witness, or agent) or their  
character, to the extent revealed in their conduct during the case, is also  
protected from being considered defamation.  
o Opinion on Public Performances: Expressing a good-faith opinion about  
the merits of a performance submitted to public judgment or sharing an  
opinion about the author's character, as evident in the performance, is not  
considered defamation. This protection applies when the author voluntarily  
submits the performance to public judgment, either explicitly or through  
actions implying such submission.  
o Censure by Authority: A person with authority over another, either  
conferred by law or arising from a lawful contract, is not engaging in  
defamation when passing, in good faith, any censure on the conduct of the  
other party in matters related to the lawful authority.  
o Good Faith Accusation to Lawful Authority: Preferring, in good faith, an  
accusation against any person to those who have lawful authority over that  
person regarding the subject matter of the accusation is not considered  
defamation.  
o Imputation for Protection of Interests: Making an imputation on the  
character of another is not defamation if it is done in good faith for the  
protection of the interests of the person making it, or of any other person,  
or for the public good.  
o Protection for Cautions: Conveying a caution in good faith, aimed at the  
welfare of the person to whom it is conveyed, or of someone in whom that  
person has an interest, or for the public good, is not considered defamation.  
38
